question: Your team uses Claude Code in a pipeline that writes docstrings for functions across several services. Each docstring receives a confidence score, and the pipeline commits docstrings above a threshold without human review. The team wants to measure the ongoing error rate of these high-confidence docstrings and to detect error patterns that it has never seen before. Which approach best meets this goal?

options.text: Have reviewers check only the docstrings that developers later report as wrong in pull request comments.
options.reason: This sample is neither random nor stratified, so it gives a biased error rate and cannot systematically detect novel error patterns as the guide describes.

options.text: Have reviewers regularly check a stratified random sample of high-confidence docstrings, drawn from each service and function type.
options.reason: The guide names stratified random sampling of high-confidence outputs as the method for ongoing error rate measurement and novel error pattern detection.

options.text: Send only the low-confidence docstrings to reviewers, because docstrings above the threshold have already proven reliable.
options.reason: This leaves the error rate of high-confidence docstrings unmeasured, and the guide requires sampling them to catch errors and novel patterns.

options.text: Track one overall acceptance rate for all docstrings and raise the threshold only if that rate drops.
options.reason: The guide warns that an aggregate accuracy metric can mask poor performance on specific segments, so it cannot reliably reveal segment errors or new patterns.
